# 🚀 Get started

📦 **Data**: [FAO Global Capture
Production](https://www.fao.org/fishery/collection/capture/en), release
**2026.1.0** (published by FAO on 2026-03-30; catches 1950–2024),
downloaded from
[Capture_2026.1.0.zip](https://www.fao.org/fishery/static/Data/Capture_2026.1.0.zip).
Licence [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).
[`fao_data_info()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/fao_data_info.md)
shows the release you use and how to cite it.

**faofishingreport** turns the FAO Global Capture Production statistics
into charts, maps and tables for reports. This page walks through a
complete first analysis of the **Northeast Atlantic (FAO major fishing
area 27)**; every chart below was produced by the code shown above it.

A typical workflow:

| Step | What you do | Functions |
|----|----|----|
| 1\. Data | Check for and download the latest FAO release; see which release you use | [`check_fao_update()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/check_fao_update.md), [`download_fao_data()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/download_fao_data.md), [`fao_data_info()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/fao_data_info.md) |
| 2\. Fishing area | Total catch, main species and main countries of an area | [`fishing_area_data()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/fishing_area_data.md), [`fishing_area_species()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/fishing_area_species.md), [`fishing_area_country()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/fishing_area_country.md) |
| 3\. Species and countries | Who catches a species, what a country catches | [`species_country()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/species_country.md), [`country_species()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/country_species.md), [`country_analysis()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/country_analysis.md) |
| 4\. Summaries | Composition, stock status, trends, data quality, diversity, fleets | [`species_group_composition()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/species_group_composition.md), [`stock_status()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/stock_status.md), [`peak_trend()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/peak_trend.md), [`data_quality()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/data_quality.md), [`coastal_distant()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/coastal_distant.md), … |
| 5\. Methods from the literature | Catch shocks, collapses, synchrony, pelagic/demersal ratio, mean temperature of the catch | [`catch_shocks()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/catch_shocks.md), [`collapse_analysis()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/collapse_analysis.md), [`catch_synchrony()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/catch_synchrony.md), [`pelagic_demersal()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/pelagic_demersal.md), [`mean_temperature_catch()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/mean_temperature_catch.md) |
| 6\. Stock assessment | CMSY++ for the main species | [`cmsy_setup()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_setup.md), [`cmsy_area()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_area.md) |
| 7\. Report | A Word report of an area in one call | [`fao_report()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/fao_report.md) |
| 8\. Style | Language, theme, colours, map projection | [`fao_settings()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/fao_settings.md) |

## 📦 Installation

faofishingreport needs **R 4.2 or later**. Install it from GitHub:

``` r

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("Linbojun99/faofishingreport", dependencies = TRUE)
```

With `dependencies = TRUE` every package that the analyses use is
installed with it: dplyr, ggplot2 and sf for the charts and maps,
rnaturalearth for the world maps, officer and xml2 for Word reports,
eoffice for editable PowerPoint charts, nanoparquet for the FishBase and
SeaLifeBase tables, ncdf4 for sea surface temperature files, and the R
packages of CMSY++ (coda, conicfit, gplots, MASS, mvtnorm, neuralnet,
…). The only exceptions are rjags and R2jags, which need the separate
JAGS program:
[`cmsy_setup()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/cmsy_setup.md)
installs JAGS and both packages the first time you use CMSY++ (see [📉
CMSY++ stock
assessment](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/articles/cmsy.md)).

**Windows and macOS** use binary packages, so no compiler (Rtools) is
needed. On macOS, editable PowerPoint charts also need
[XQuartz](https://www.xquartz.org). **Linux** needs the system libraries
of the sf package and, for Chinese charts, a Chinese font:

``` bash
sudo apt-get install libgdal-dev libgeos-dev libproj-dev libudunits2-dev fonts-noto-cjk
```

Load the package. The start-up message shows the operating system and
the font chosen for charts (SimSun on Windows, Songti SC on macOS, Noto
Serif CJK SC on Linux):

``` r

library(faofishingreport)
#> faofishingreport: Windows, chart font "SimSun" (change it with fao_font())
```

## 💾 Get the latest FAO data

The package comes with FAO release 2026.1.0. FAO publishes a new release
about once a year. Check whether a newer one exists and download it
(about 5 MB, a few seconds):

``` r

check_fao_update()
#> FAO Global Capture Production
#>   Latest online release: 2026.1.0 (published 2026-03-30)
#>   Bundled with package:  2026.1.0
#>   Downloaded locally:    none
#>   Your data is up to date.

download_fao_data()   # only needed when a newer release is available
```

All functions automatically use the newest data available.
[`fao_data_info()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/fao_data_info.md)
tells which release that is, where it comes from and how to cite it. See
[💾 FAO
data](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/articles/data.md)
for all the arguments of these functions, choosing releases, the data
format and working with your own subsets.

## 📁 Where the results go

Each analysis saves its charts and tables in the **current working
folder**:

| Folder | Content |
|----|----|
| `figures/png/` | Charts as PNG (always); the summary analyses use `figures/png/summary/` |
| `figures/pptx/` | Charts as editable PowerPoint files (with `pptx = TRUE`; uses the eoffice package) |
| `tables/` | Tables as CSV, readable by Excel including Chinese names |
| `reports/` | Word reports of [`fao_report()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/fao_report.md) |

So start by choosing a folder for the report:

``` r

setwd("D:/reports/FAO27")   # any folder
```

## 🌊 First analysis: FAO area 27

[`fishing_area_data()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/fishing_area_data.md)
extracts the catch of one FAO major fishing area and draws its total
catch with the breakpoints of the mean catch, its share of the world
catch of all marine areas, and a world map of the countries fishing
there.

``` r

FAO27 <- fishing_area_data("Atlantic, Northeast")
```

![fishing_trend.png](data:image/png;base64,)

![fishing_percentage.png](data:image/png;base64,)

![area_country_map.png](data:image/png;base64,)

The result is a list with the catch records of the area (`area_data`),
the periods between breakpoints (`coefs_data`) and the map data
(`act_world_map`). `FAO27$area_data` is the input of most other
functions:

``` r

show_table(FAO27$area_data, n = 5)
```

|  | Country..Name. | ASFIS.species..Name. | FAO.major.fishing.area..Name. | Unit..Name. | Unit | Year | Production | Production.Type |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|---:|:---|
| 51634 | Belgium | European eel | Atlantic, Northeast | Tonnes - live weight | TLW, Number | 2018 | 1.0 | actual |
| 51635 | Belgium | European eel | Atlantic, Northeast | Tonnes - live weight | TLW, Number | 2019 | 1.0 | actual |
| 51636 | Belgium | European eel | Atlantic, Northeast | Tonnes - live weight | TLW, Number | 2020 | 0.7 | actual |
| 51637 | Belgium | European eel | Atlantic, Northeast | Tonnes - live weight | TLW, Number | 2021 | 1.0 | actual |
| 51638 | Belgium | European eel | Atlantic, Northeast | Tonnes - live weight | TLW, Number | 2022 | 0.0 | actual |

Any other area works the same way. The names of the FAO major fishing
areas are:

``` r

data <- load_fao_data()
sort(unique(data$FAO.major.fishing.area..Name.))
#>  [1] "Africa - Inland waters"           "America, North - Inland waters"  
#>  [3] "America, South - Inland waters"   "Arctic Sea"                      
#>  [5] "Asia - Inland waters"             "Atlantic, Antarctic"             
#>  [7] "Atlantic, Eastern Central"        "Atlantic, Northeast"             
#>  [9] "Atlantic, Northwest"              "Atlantic, Southeast"             
#> [11] "Atlantic, Southwest"              "Atlantic, Western Central"       
#> [13] "Europe - Inland waters"           "Former USSR area - Inland waters"
#> [15] "Indian Ocean, Antarctic"          "Indian Ocean, Eastern"           
#> [17] "Indian Ocean, Western"            "Mediterranean and Black Sea"     
#> [19] "Oceania - Inland waters"          "Pacific, Antarctic"              
#> [21] "Pacific, Eastern Central"         "Pacific, Northeast"              
#> [23] "Pacific, Northwest"               "Pacific, Southeast"              
#> [25] "Pacific, Southwest"               "Pacific, Western Central"
```

## 🐟 Main species and countries

The ten species with the largest catch in area 27, their catch over time
and the breakpoints of their mean catch:

``` r

species <- fishing_area_species(FAO27$area_data, rank_range = 1:10)
```

![area_species.png](data:image/png;base64,)

![area_species_wrap.png](data:image/png;base64,)

The same for the countries:

``` r

countries <- fishing_area_country(FAO27$area_data, rank_range = 1:10)
```

![area_country.png](data:image/png;base64,)

![area_country_wrap.png](data:image/png;base64,)

`rank_range` lists the ranks shown: `1:10` the first ten, `11:20` the
next ten, `c(5, 6)` the fifth and the sixth.

## 🖥️ What you see in the console

When a function finishes, it shows a short summary of its results in the
console: what was analysed, the first rows of its main table, the charts
and tables it saved, and the parts of the result it returns. The result
itself is returned invisibly: assign it (`species <- ...`) to keep it.
Here the fifth and the sixth species:

``` r

fao_settings(show_data = TRUE)   # the default (the articles of this site turn it off)
species56 <- fishing_area_species(FAO27$area_data, rank_range = c(5, 6))
#> 
#> ── fishing_area_species(): Atlantic, Northeast ─────────────────────────────────
#> Ranks 5 to 6 of 1029 species items, by catch over all years (catch_t and share_pct: all years):
#>  rank                   species    catch_t share_pct
#>     5 Atlantic mackerel         44,615,940      6.19
#>     6 Sandeels(=Sandlances) nei 33,532,765      4.65
#> Charts saved in figures/png/area/: area_species.png, area_species_wrap.png
#> Tables saved in tables/: species_ranked_table.csv, species_coefs_data.csv
#> Results returned: $area_species, $area_species_ranked, $area_species_ranked_total, $coefs_data
fao_settings(show_data = FALSE)
```

`plot_show = TRUE` also draws each chart in the plot window (the Plots
pane of RStudio) as it is saved; `plot = TRUE` keeps saving the chart
files either way:

``` r

species <- fishing_area_species(FAO27$area_data, rank_range = 1:10, plot_show = TRUE)
fao_settings(plot_show = TRUE)    # every function of the session draws its charts
fao_settings(show_data = FALSE)   # no summaries in the console
```

## 🌐 Chinese and bilingual charts

Every analysis has a `lang` argument: `"en"` (English), `"zh"` (Chinese)
or `"both"`. Country, species and area names use the official FAO
Chinese names.

``` r

species_country(FAO27$area_data, species_name = "Atlantic cod", lang = "both")
```

![Atlantic_cod_country_ranked_wrap.png](data:image/png;base64,)

To use Chinese everywhere, set it once with `fao_settings(lang = "zh")`.

## 📊 A first summary: stock status

[`stock_status()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/stock_status.md)
classifies each species by its catch relative to its peak catch (stock
status plots, Kleisner et al. 2013):

``` r

status <- stock_status(FAO27$area_data)
```

![Atlantic\_\_Northeast_stock_status_stocks.png](data:image/png;base64,)

![Atlantic\_\_Northeast_stock_status_catch.png](data:image/png;base64,)

## 📝 A Word report in one call

[`fao_report()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/fao_report.md)
runs the analyses of an area and writes a Word report with cover,
abstract, data sources and methods, results with charts and tables,
conclusions, references and appendix tables. The area can be given by
its name or its code:

``` r

fao_report(27, lang = "en")   # writes reports/FAO27_report_en.docx in the working folder
```

By default the report has the total catch and its stages, the main
species and countries, the ISSCAAP groups, the stock status plots, the
data quality, the diversity of the catch and the coastal and
distant-water fleets. Catch shocks, collapses, synchrony, the
pelagic/demersal ratio, the mean temperature of the catch, distant-water
fleet profiles and CMSY++ can be switched on. See [📝 Assessment report:
Word, LaTeX and
PDF](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/articles/report.md)
for all its settings.

## ⚙️ Settings of the functions on this page

The arguments shared by the analyses:

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|----|----|----|
| `lang` | Language of the chart text and names: `"en"`, `"zh"` or `"both"` | `NULL`: the language of [`fao_settings()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/fao_settings.md) (`"en"` unless changed) |
| `plot` | Save the charts | `TRUE` |
| `table` | Save the tables in `tables/` (not in [`fishing_area_data()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/fishing_area_data.md)) | `TRUE` |
| `pptx` | Also save the charts as editable PowerPoint files | `FALSE`, or `pptx` of [`fao_settings()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/fao_settings.md) |
| `plot_show` | Also draw each chart in the plot window (e.g. the Plots pane of RStudio) as it is saved | `FALSE`, or `plot_show` of [`fao_settings()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/fao_settings.md) |
| `ZH` | Older way of asking for Chinese: `ZH = TRUE` is `lang = "zh"` (only in the fishing area, species and country functions) | `FALSE` |
| `label` | Name used in the output files of the summary analyses, e.g. [`stock_status()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/stock_status.md) | `NULL`: the fishing area (or country) of the data |

Every function has its own arguments as well; each article has a table
of all of them:

| Functions | Main arguments | All arguments |
|----|----|----|
| [`check_fao_update()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/check_fao_update.md), [`download_fao_data()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/download_fao_data.md), [`load_fao_data()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/load_fao_data.md), [`fao_data_info()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/fao_data_info.md) | `version`, `data_dir`, `overwrite`, `quiet` | [💾 FAO data](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/articles/data.md) |
| [`fishing_area_data()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/fishing_area_data.md) | `area_name`, `timeseries_analysis`, `data_version`, colours and text sizes | [🌊 Fishing area analysis](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/articles/fishing-areas.md) |
| [`fishing_area_species()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/fishing_area_species.md), [`fishing_area_country()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/fishing_area_country.md) | `rank_range`, `timeseries_analysis`, `h_value`, line and text styles | [🌊 Fishing area analysis](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/articles/fishing-areas.md) |
| [`species_country()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/species_country.md) | `species_name`, `rank_range`, `h_value`, map style | [🐟 Species and countries](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/articles/species-countries.md) |
| [`stock_status()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/stock_status.md) | `taxon_levels`, `min_years`, `min_consecutive`, `min_catch`, `smooth` | [📈 Composition, stock status and trends](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/articles/status-trends.md) |
| [`fao_report()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/fao_report.md) | `area`, `lang`, `file`, sections switched on or off, settings of each analysis | [📝 Assessment report: Word, LaTeX and PDF](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/articles/report.md) |
| [`fao_settings()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/fao_settings.md), [`fao_font()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/fao_font.md) | `lang`, `theme`, `palette`, `map_projection`, `dpi`, … | [🎨 Customise charts and maps](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/articles/customise.md) |
